model: MicroTech 4 Rebel Applied Rooftop Unit Controller
applies_to: Daikin Rebel Applied (DPSA) packaged rooftop units with the MicroTech 4 unit controller.
summary: The MicroTech 4 controller on Rebel Applied (DPSA) rooftops joins BACnet IP or BACnet MS/TP through a plug-in communication module (a LonWorks module is the third option; only BACnet objects are listed here). Objects cover unit and occupancy status, network enables for cooling, heating and the economizer, temperatures and refrigerant readings, supply and return fan control, dehumidification, outdoor air, run hours, optional refrigerant, power and IAQ monitoring, expansion-board I/O, read-only unit configuration and alarm/event BIs. Most writable inputs only apply when AHU Loc/Net (MV 19) is set to Network at the HMI.
notes: Needs a BACnet IP or BACnet MS/TP communication module on the controller; the LonWorks module objects are not listed.
AHU Loc/Net (MV 19) must be Network for most writable network points to apply; it can only be changed at the HMI.
Points depend on unit configuration and options: variable compressors, ECM or VFD fans, energy recovery, refrigerant, power and IAQ monitoring packages, and the expansion I/O board.
Alarm BIs (Table 37) read 0=Normal/1=In Alarm or 0=Open/1=Closed as marked; event BIs (Tables 38-39) flag active control events. Notification classes NC 1-4 are Faults, Problems, Warnings and Events.
This file covers the MicroTech 4 controller. Rebel DPS and DPH units on the earlier MicroTech controller are covered by the MicroTech III Applied Rooftop and Self-Contained list (ED 15112).
Range text lists English and SI units; English units are shown here.

integration.summary: Set AHU Loc/Net to Network at the HMI, then drive the unit with Occupancy Mode or Current State, plus Application Mode and the occupied setpoints. Use Emergency Override to stop the unit from the network, and read Unit State, unit status, capacities, temperatures and the alarm objects.

minimum_points.name: CurrentState
minimum_points.why: Occupancy Scheduler Input when Occupancy Mode is Auto

minimum_points.name: AHULoc/Net
minimum_points.why: Must read Network for network inputs to apply

integration.enable: AHU Loc/Net (MV 19) must be set to Network at the HMI (it is read-only over BACnet) for most network inputs to apply. Occupancy is then commanded with Occupancy Mode (MV 7) or, when MV 7 is Auto, Current State (MV 8). Emergency Override (MV 10) = Off shuts the unit off (Unit Status OffNet) and only writing Normal restarts it. Application Mode (MV 5) only acts when Control Mode is Auto, which is set at the HMI. Cooling, heating and economizer can be enabled or capped from the network with AV 36/37, AV 38/39 and AV 34/35 (Ctrl Mode = Auto).
integration.heartbeat: No BACnet heartbeat (Receive Heartbeat is listed as N/A for BACnet IP and MS/TP). Values written by the BAS stay at the last valid value if communication is lost; an invalid network value makes the controller use its default, and network sensor inputs fall back to the local sensor.
integration.remote_sensors: Space Temperature Input (AV 31) and Outdoor Air Temperature Input (AV 32) take network temperatures and revert to the local sensor if the network value becomes unreliable. Network inputs also exist for space humidity (AV 20/21), space CO2 (AV 33), supply and return fan capacity (AV 24/25) and outdoor air damper minimum and maximum position (AV 17/55). A LonWorks value takes precedence over the BACnet one if both are present.
setup: Initial device instance is calculated from the production code (IP) or MAC address (MS/TP); change it at the HMI and set Apply Changes in the BACnet IP or MS/TP setup menu (the controller restarts).
BACnet IP defaults: DHCP on, given IP 127.0.0.1, mask 255.255.255.0, UDP port 47808.
BACnet MS/TP defaults: MAC address 18, 38400 baud, Max Master 127, Max Info Frames 1.
MS/TP terminating resistor is an HMI setting (Term Resistor) and is lost at power-off; a physical resistor is recommended.
If the BAS cannot subscribe to the notification class recipient lists, enter its device instance in NC Dev 1 or NC Dev 2 in the BACnet setup menu and cycle power.
gotchas: Multistate objects that are also unit configuration code items read with an extra '(n)' at the end of the state text over BACnet, e.g. 'OnOffT(1)'.
ClearAlarms (MV 13) clears by class and returns to No once the alarms clear; write it only to clear an active alarm.
Network Demand Shed Enable (MV 22) only works when DemandShed is also enabled in the HMI HtgClg ChgOvr Set-Up menu.
The guide prints MV 37 twice: RFEF1Status (ECM return fan 1) and VFD_RFEFStatus (return fan VFD: 1=OK, 2=Fault, 3=No Comm). Only RFEF1Status is listed; check the object name on the unit.
The refrigerant monitoring table names AI 50 and AI 60 C1DischLnTemp and C2DischLnTemp; the main table calls them C1DischLnTemp1 and C2DischLnTemp2.
The BACnet module and controller clocks re-sync about every 60-68 minutes, so BACnet date/time can differ for a while after a keypad change.
